test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

I **have** visited Delhi last year.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "I have visited Delhi last year" is incorrect because the present perfect tense (have visited) should not be used with a specific time reference like "last year."
 
• The past simple tense ("visited") is the appropriate choice when referring to completed actions in the past with a specific time mentioned.
 
• Other options like "had visited" or "was visiting" do not fit the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I visited Delhi last year."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "had visited"** – This is incorrect as the past perfect tense is used when there are two past events and this sentence mentions only one.
 
• **Option 3: "was visiting"** – This is incorrect as the past continuous tense is used for actions in progress in the past, which does not apply here.
 
• **Option 4: "did visit"** – While grammatically correct, it is usually used for emphasis and is unnecessary here.
